name: Geaest
prior: UPIC lineage: UPISketch (Centre Iannis Xenakis 2018; UPISketch2 free iPad app that lets users 'freely draw absolute pitch curves', v2 added 'live synthesis' and 'smoother pitch glissandi', v3.5 via Gumroad; VS: apps.apple.com id1461075546, maci.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/en/node/343, forum.juce.com UPISketch), HighC (Thomas Baudel 1991-2015, additive, UPIC-inspired; VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HighC), IanniX (VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPIC) = drawn glissandi as composition tools, not voices. Photophore (Taika Systems, iPad 2014): 'flock synthesis', up to 100 oscillators per patch, 'a behavioral algorithm and physics simulation keeps the oscillators in tune with each other while still permitting some natural drift and detuning', flocking tendency/avoidance/speed/turbulence, touch 'fleeing' = extreme pitch modulation, mono glide, 6-voice poly (VS: apps.apple.com id937318617, synthtopia.com 2014/12/10, sonicstate.com 2014/12/11, cdm.link; R: musicians.md 2.8) = the closest playable prior: agents in pitch space pulled back to tune. Dewanatron Swarmatron (8 oscillators under one ribbon, 'swarm' flows in and out of unison, adjustable spacing) and reFuse 'The Swarm' free emulation 2014 (VS: wikipedia Swarmatron, cdm.link); Radikal RT-311 Swarm Oscillator (Eurorack, clones pitched to 'musical intervals, clusters, or detuned arrangements'; VS: perfectcircuit.com); Mille (Sancristoforo 2023, 1000 oscillators, standalone drone synth; VS: synthanatomy.com 2023/07, synthtopia.com p=137306); Dillon Bastan Songbird (M4L boids flock as modulation + syrinx voices; VS: isotonikstudios.com). Sampled: Spitfire Orchestral Swarm (players' random short notes on one pitch = pointillist cloud) and Swarms (glissandi; VS: rekkerd.org p=117843, recordingmag.com). History: Xenakis 'drew the glissandi as straight lines' in Metastasis 1953/54 (VS: UPISketch chapter, books.openbookpublishers.com obp.0390); Ligeti/Penderecki cluster bands (A). In Myzel: Nebel (static +-12 ct unison, LFO on detune, APP 3543), Schwarm (FM insects). Not found: straight-line glissandi that branch from shared points and return to the played note with the fan width under a finger.
costNotes: Native: 6 OscillatorNodes + 6 Gains + lowpass + out ~ 14 nodes x 0.03 = 0.42 units (R: webaudio.md section 4), L3 12 lines + 2 panners ~ 0.85; the idea's 'nativ ~ 0.7' is high. The glissandi are exact and free natively: osc.detune.linearRampToValueAtTime(q_i x 100, t_arrive) is a straight line in semitones (cents are log-frequency), the Gestik bus stays on detune (v.mod, APP 3464), setF glides osc.frequency underneath, 'sawtooth' is band-limited by the browser and 'Glas' is a cached PeriodicWave (A.waves, APP 3781); retargeting needs ~6 events/s per voice from a lookahead timer (the 25-ms worker clock exists, APP 6043-6044). Worklet: 6 table oscillators = 21.8 ns/sample = 0.18 units (M: research/bench/grain_osc_cost.js) + node 0.06 + 3 params 0.09 + 2-pole lowpass ~ 0.35, L3 12 lines + stereo ~ 0.6 - cheaper and with sample-accurate per-line pan, but the band-limited saw must be built per octave and the module dependency appears. Recommendation: native first (no worklet, no aliasing work, Firefox k-rate caveat irrelevant since ramps are events), worklet only if per-line pan at L3 is wanted.
soundHeld: y = fan width. At y ~ 0.15 (sigma_eff ~ 1 semitone with heimkehr 0.5) it is a slowly moving chorus with a clear pitch - the best register, warmer than Nebel because the detunes move, cross and briefly unite; at y ~ 0.5 (sigma_eff ~ 3.6 HT, lines wander +-4 HT) the pitch centre is only statistical: a Ligeti cluster at tempo 1-3 HT/s, sirens at tempo 20 - a texture, not a melodic voice; at y = 0 six identical triangles are one dead triangle (give y = 0 a floor of +-4 ct and 0.3 HT/s). Branch points are audible only as beat-free unison moments followed by re-opening beating (a zip), subtle but real at p = 0.3 with 6 lines; the 'straight line' geometry itself is not perceptible against curved glissandi - it is a composer's truth, not a listener's. The waveform is static (triangle/saw), so timbre does not follow Hoehe as Myzel's convention expects (R: musicians.md 7.1); the 8 f lowpass needs a Hoehe-coupled cutoff or saw by default. Several fingers = 18-36 gliding lines = mush beyond two (as with Strudel). Gestik tilt opening the fan on a held chord is the strongest gesture here.
soundBurst: All lines start in unison, sigma opens over the gate, speed x4: at tempo 3 (12 HT/s) a 160-ms gate ends with a 1-2 HT fan that keeps opening through the 1.5-s release - a note that splits into a trail ('Pfeil'), distinctive, tempo-robust, and the reverse (lines converging into unison) would be a second burst mode for free. Weakness: no transient (burstEnv att >= 3 ms on a triangle = soft, APP 3517), so Puls lanes need the saw colour or a 10-ms noise tick; at tempo 24 the x4 (96 HT/s = 8 oct/s) is a laser zap - clamp the burst speed at 24 HT/s. At 1/16 120 bpm the fan opens only during the release, which overlaps the next hit (two trails) - acceptable, even pretty.
failureModes: No pitch identity above y ~ 0.4: a melodic line played high in the field dissolves into a cluster - the catalogue must call it a texture/drone engine, and Gestik Hoehe offsets must be capped
y = 0 is a dead unison triangle; needs a detune floor and minimal motion
Static waveform: Hoehe does not change timbre (Myzel convention) - couple the lowpass or add formant motion
Branching geometry is inaudible as such (only unison moments are); the novelty is on paper unless lines are also drawn on screen
Puls hits lack a transient; burst needs saw/tick and a speed clamp (24 HT/s)
Polyphony mush: 3+ fingers x 6 lines; cap lines to 4 per voice when > 2 voices of this engine are alive
Native retargeting via timers: a missed timer (background tab) freezes a line at its target - schedule the next target 200 ms ahead and always have a fallback ramp queued
verdict: Rare: drawn straight-line glissandi are the UPIC family (UPISketch2 is a free iPad app with live synthesis), swarm oscillators under a ribbon are the Swarmatron/RT-311, and Photophore (iPad 2014) already plays flocking oscillators that drift and are pulled back to tune - Geaest's branching ruled surfaces with homecoming are a new geometry on known ground. Native-feasible at ~0.45 units (L3 ~0.85): linear detune ramps are exact straight glissandi, band-limited saws come free and the Gestik bus stays on detune, so no worklet is needed (a worklet would be ~0.35/0.6). Musically it is a texture engine with a sweet melodic register at low fan width; above y ~ 0.4 held notes have no pitch identity, the static waveform ignores Hoehe-as-timbre, and the Puls 'Pfeil' is good but transient-less - keep it with a y floor, a Hoehe-coupled filter and a saw/tick for bursts, and sell it as cluster/drone, not as a lead.
